body:
## Summary

During post-install/re-entry inspection on `release/0.33.0-dev`, installed systemd units still carried `Version: 0.32.1` headers and depended on multiple `*-hotfix-*` drop-ins.

This is an install/release packaging hygiene issue. For a prod-ready 0.33.0 installation, required runtime fixes should be integrated into the canonical unit files or explicitly installed as supported override units with clear versioning. The installed unit surface should not look like a stack of temporary hotfixes from earlier recovery work.

## Environment

- NoemaForge CLI: `0.33.0`
- Branch: `release/0.33.0-dev`
- Installed path: `/etc/systemd/system/noemaforge-*.service`
- Runtime profile used during re-entry: `runtime_only`

## Evidence

`systemctl cat noemaforge-llm-gateway.service` showed the canonical unit header still says:

```text
# File: systemd/noemaforge-llm-gateway.service
# Zone: release/package
# Version: 0.32.1
# Created: 2026-05-14
# Modified: 2026-05-14
```

The same installed gateway unit also relies on drop-ins:

```text
/etc/systemd/system/noemaforge-llm-gateway.service.d/90-hotfix-no-state-directory.conf
/etc/systemd/system/noemaforge-llm-gateway.service.d/95-socket-path-hotfix.conf
```

`noemaforge-toolproxy.service` had several override drop-ins:

```text
/etc/systemd/system/noemaforge-toolproxy.service.d/05-sel-perms.conf
/etc/systemd/system/noemaforge-toolproxy.service.d/10-root-preflight.conf
/etc/systemd/system/noemaforge-toolproxy.service.d/90-hotfix-no-state-directory.conf
/etc/systemd/system/noemaforge-toolproxy.service.d/95-socket-path-hotfix.conf
```

Runtime was working with these drop-ins, but that is exactly the concern: the installed package appears to require accumulated local hotfixes rather than a clean 0.33.0 service definition.

## Expected behavior

For 0.33.0 release/install:

```text
- systemd unit headers should match the release version or avoid stale version metadata.
- Required fixes should be integrated into canonical unit files.
- Supported override files, if intentionally used, should have stable names and documentation, not “hotfix” names.
- setup/install should be able to recreate a working systemd surface from a clean machine without relying on old local drop-ins.
```

## Suggested fix

1. Review all `/etc/systemd/system/noemaforge*.service*` outputs from clean install.
2. Move required `RuntimeDirectory`, `StateDirectory`, socket-path, SEL permission, and preflight fixes into canonical unit files or documented supported drop-ins.
3. Update unit file headers/version metadata for 0.33.0.
4. Add an install verification check that reports unexpected `*-hotfix-*` drop-ins after clean install.
5. Add a clean-install CI/release test that runs `systemctl cat` and verifies the expected unit/drop-in layout.

## Why this matters

A prod-ready installer should produce a reproducible, explainable systemd surface. If the working system depends on stale hotfix overrides, future installs, upgrades, and debugging sessions can diverge from the tested environment.
title: 0.33.0 installed systemd units still rely on hotfix drop-ins and stale 0.32.1 unit metadata
